formation.explanation: Node batches proposals into Peer under raftMu. Leader stamps term/index, replicates to members and advances commitment from voting match order statistic only for its current term. Followers require preceding term match and protect the committed prefix, replying after engine persistence. Conflicts reduce next and retry; snapshots resynchronize missing history. Engine exposes committed entries to the RSM queue, whose application/session results and applied index drive client consumption. ReadIndex separately samples committed index, gathers heartbeat confirmation and releases pending prefixes to local readiness or remote responses.

context.explanation: Per-cluster term, role and applied membership define authority. Timers launch elections for eligible full members only after committed work is applied; votes require fresh log and no conflicting vote. Candidate quorum promotes and appends a current-term no-op. Higher terms demote/reset; lower terms are rejected. CheckQuorum may revoke leadership; transfer waits for target match and uses TimeoutNow, while proposals are dropped during transfer. Configuration application changes participant maps and local removal revokes leadership. Restart restores persisted term/vote/log but initializes transient follower context.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch precedes response consumption. Reset clears old votes, replication progress and pending ReadIndex support while retaining established log/commit; leader must form current-term commitment before multi-voter reads. Log freshness and committed-prefix protection constrain future leaders. Election waits for application so committed membership changes affect later quorums; RSM changes update Peer under raftMu. Old client work can be dropped or time out independently of preserved decisions. Read confirmation is transient; exact context and applied-index checks bridge its publication to requester completion, but remote prefix publication substitutes the confirming context for earlier remote requests. Ordinary configuration callbacks complete before visible batch lastApplied publication; snapshot recovery instead publishes its visible index before RestoreRemotes. Whether a step can use that interval for election is an open authority premise.

feedback.answered: Controller assessment confirms the scoped read-prefix identity violation after correspondence review. Ordinary applied-index publication was then traced: setApplied only advances internal index/term; setLastApplied publishes the visible index after handleEntry returns, so ApplyConfigChange precedes visibility. Snapshot recovery differs: apply writes lastApplied before Recover calls RestoreRemotes; the latter competes for raftMu with the initialized node step worker. This leaves a distinct sourced authority-transition question, without assuming that the available locks fail in a legal history.
remaining: Construct a legal initialized snapshot recovery overlap and inspect whether an election uses old membership.
